case.summary: Case HHG-018 stays uncertain at fraud probability 0.60 for the $39.08 in-person purchase (txn 3491361, product W, region 126.0) that customer C02354 denies. The episode also pulls in a preceding same-window transaction, 3490180 ($117.07, region 325.0, 2016-11-27 window), for a combined exposure of $156.15; the label defaults to the convention pattern out_of_region_use, though a reasonable alternative reading is account_takeover, since neither episode region is actually novel for the card (126.0 has 566 prior visits, hint=known; 325.0 is the modal region itself). The decisive fraud-side evidence is the customer-family denial (trigger) plus the memory family's 19 prior confirmed-fraud closed cases on this same card (a mix of account_takeover and out_of_region_use, most recently CC-5558 on 2016-11-01), and the standout cms_p=0.72 on chain member 3490180 versus a chain baseline under 0.02; the decisive legitimacy-side evidence is the history family showing the amount and both regions fit the card's normal baseline, and recurring_charge_check's near-miss on R7 (17 prior same-price hits at 126.0, but gap_cv=1.03 fails the ≤0.6 cadence test, so no automatic recurring-charge exemption applied). We asked the customer (customer_validation) to confirm which transactions in the window were theirs and assumed, per §5, a simulated no-reply within 24 hours; that non-answer triggers R4, so the recommendation is MONITOR_CARD plus DECLINE_TRANSACTION (route L1) on any further authorizations on card C02354-K2 while the case (auto, CREATE_CASE) stays open and is escalated to analyst review (auto, ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST) under R8 for the still-conflicting evidence; no block or SAR is warranted yet. Similar closed cases CC-1699 (confirmed account_takeover on this same card) and CC-4356/CC-4996 (confirmed out_of_region_use, same region) both informed the pattern read and the decision to keep the card's own case history weighted heavily in the score.
